snapshot.readinessLevel: Good — Oura 70 at wake. Sleep is strong (8.7h) but body temp is +0.45° and rising three days running, with HRV at 44. Treat the quality day as conditional.

change: The gray zone is still where your training lives: over the last 30 days, 45% of your running time (376 min, 37.6 mi) sat in Z3 versus 44% genuinely easy. The last 14 days are better — 49% easy / 39% gray / 12% hard — so it is moving in the right direction.

The long run is now the single biggest lever. Aug 1's 10-miler averaged 128 bpm, which looks perfect on paper, but 48 of its 105 minutes were actually in Z3. The average hides the drift — walk the hills and take a 60-second break whenever you cross 132.

Anaerobic load is above target (571 against a 173–519 band) and aerobic-low is over too (966 vs 398–917), while aerobic-high sits near the bottom of its range (595 of 554–1073). The gap is filled by steady threshold work and more genuinely easy volume, not by more hard intervals.

Recovery is quietly softening. Garmin resting HR drifted 47 → 52 over two weeks, training status slipped Productive → Maintaining, and Oura shows body temp +0.45° with HRV at 44. None of those alone is alarming; together they say hold this week rather than build.
continue: Long-run HR control is real progress. Jul 25's 9-miler ran 61 of 93 minutes easy and Aug 1's 10-miler ran 57 of 105. Compare Jul 18's 9-miler, which managed 10 easy minutes out of 94. Same distances, completely different runs.

Volume built cleanly across three weeks — 23.1 → 25.4 → 26.7 mi — with acute:chronic load still optimal at 1.0 (acute 548, chronic 538). That is a well-executed ramp toward the 40–50 mi/wk base you need for next October.

Your quality days stay genuinely hard. Jul 28's session put 23 of 54 minutes in Z4–Z5 and Jul 22 hit 22 of 46. You are not fooling yourself about intensity — the problem is the easy days, not the hard ones.
Sleep has turned around at exactly the right time. Oura logged 8.6h and 8.7h the last two nights after a rough 5–6h stretch mid-July. Bank that while you can, with the baby due late this month.
